parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the island has its own parliament and statute book, and the governing state's equality and single-sex service rules reach it only by order, so none are operative here. Documented positives include a 2022 anti-discrimination act (in force from October 2023) covering sexual orientation, a 2005 employment ordinance covering gender identity, child-welfare protections, legal gender change since 2007, and marriage passed 37-7. Documented exposures are mild: a latent male-only private-life offence with no documented enforcement, and birth-sex records that are not amended. Border, custody placement and street-violence practice are not documented, so these are open questions, not confirmed exposures. Rated as reduced-to-low risk with uncertainty in the unresolved prison and border areas.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented entry, visa or border-screening treatment of trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border protection; no documented X or mismatch friction.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport governs entry; island legal gender change is resident-facing and does not reach visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Latent male homosexual offences for non-private acts; no documented enforcement or trans-targeted arrests.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented sexual-orientation and gender-identity anti-discrimination coverage in force from 1 October 2023.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Statute is tangential to trans status; latent male-only offence is a secondary signal only.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Only prison holds male, female and vulnerable prisoners; no birth-sex housing rule recorded but not confirmed absent.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No trans-specific segregation or solitary practice recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Parent-nation equality rules apply only by crown order; island prison is run by island government.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial or access barrier for visitors.
care_services.protection: Blood-donor rules relaxed in 2011; no trans-specific care restriction documented.
care_services.interaction: No documented interaction with border or custody pathways.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No documented state threat-framing of trans people; no documented police targeting.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Parliament and rights-charity records describe positive, unanimous institutional stance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutional acceptance points to low state threat-framing; no enforcement record to test it.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented exposure for minors or guardians travelling together.
minors_guardians.protection: Child-welfare proceedings have covered sexual orientation and gender identity since 2008 (main island) and 2016 (one smaller island).
minors_guardians.interaction: Protection is local to child-welfare proceedings and does not clearly cover travel-stage contact.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence incidents with dates or outcomes documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Anti-discrimination law and unanimous passage of the 2022 bill signal institutional commitment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of incidents is not treated as proof of safety; enforcement outcomes are not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Implementing legislation for 2015 marriage not confirmed; prison placement and border treatment unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Passed anti-discrimination statute and employment ordinance; no operative enforcement record in dossier.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions are weighted lightly; statutory protections are credited only as documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both have documented anti-discrimination protections and positive institutional stance. This dossier has documented parliamentary and statutory anti-discrimination coverage, while 0.75-A has a documented health charter and complaint office. Unresolved prison placement keeps this dossier near 0.75-A, so it sits at roughly the same level.

0.85-A has operating civilian oversight, prompt remedies and explicit gender-identity equality law with recent enforcement. This dossier has comparable law but no documented enforcement outcomes or border record, so it sits slightly lower.

0.65-B documents a refusal of care and misgendering that was remedied, and shows working complaint machinery. This dossier documents no comparable traveller-facing refusal, so it sits higher than 0.65-B.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is an island statute book with documented anti-discrimination protections in force since 2023, a 2005 gender-identity employment ordinance and positive legislative record. Exposures are limited to a latent male-only private-life offence with no documented enforcement, and an unresolved prison housing question. Border treatment, care access and street violence are not documented, so they are treated as open rather than as exposures or protections. The record is largely positive and the open questions are weighted lightly, placing the rating in the reduced-to-low risk band.
